before.headline: The product development system for teams and agents The product development system for teams and agents
before.subhead: Purpose-built for planning and building products. Designed for the AI era.

top_fixes.fix: Put a real primary button ('Start your workspace', linking to /signup, styled like the light 'Sign up' pill, 44px tall on mobile) directly under the subhead, left-aligned with the headline, with a one-line 'See plans and pricing' link to /pricing beneath it. Demote 'New Loops →' to a small badge above the headline.
top_fixes.why: Six of seven found no action in the hero: the only hero link goes to a Loops announcement, 'Sign up' is a small nav pill, and 'Get started' only appears at the very bottom.

top_fixes.fix: Replace the category label with what the demo under it shows: 'Plan and track software, from Slack thread to draft PR'. Then rename the four feature heads as outcomes in the same plain voice (e.g. 'Intake and integrations' -> 'Conversations become routed, prioritized issues').
top_fixes.why: The scroller couldn't tell what it does in 3 seconds, the copywriter and competitor both said the words are generic category copy while the Slack-to-PR demo is the real pitch.

top_fixes.fix: On mobile, cut the empty black band above the headline, drop the h1 to about 32px so it wraps in 3 lines, render the headline and subhead sharp at first paint (no blur/fade-in), and give hero links a 44px tap height so the product screenshot starts on the first screen.
top_fixes.why: The phone fold is mostly empty black plus a 4-line headline, the slow phone saw a blurred headline for 10+ seconds, and the only hero tap target is a 93x24 text link.

hero.headline: Plan and track software, from Slack thread to draft PR
hero.subhead: Turn conversations into prioritized issues and let AI agents work them alongside your team, up to a pull request ready for review. Used by 40,000+ product teams.
hero.note: See plans and pricing before you sign up →

section_order.section: Hero (new headline, subhead, button) + the DRV-8852 product demo
section_order.why: The demo is what every visitor praised; the copy now names what it shows and the hero finally asks for the click.

section_order.section: Logo strip, with 'Linear powers over 40,000 product teams. From ambitious startups to major enterprises.' moved up from the customers block as its caption
section_order.why: Replaces 'POWERING THE COMPANIES BUILDING THE FUTURE' with the page's strongest checkable-sounding line, which the copywriter found buried near the footer.
Starts the loop the headline promises: the Slack #product thread becoming issues is the ideal customer's 'every morning' task.
The agents-as-teammates section is the differentiator the competitor can't copy; it belongs right after intake.
Closes the Slack-thread-to-PR loop with the diff and review view.
Roadmaps and cycle time matter to leads but don't advance the headline's story; also needs the contrast fix the designer flagged.

section_order.section: Customers (#customers): Gabriel Peal (OpenAI) and Nik Koblov (Ramp) quotes
section_order.why: Named proof right before the ask. [NEEDS: one quote with a measurable outcome, e.g. time to ship or tool replaced, with name and company]

section_order.section: [NEEDS: plan and pricing summary: what is free, whether a card is required, paid price per seat, and how long importing from Jira takes]
section_order.why: Pricing was the top unanswered question for the burned buyer, the competitor and the ideal customer; only the owner can state these terms.

section_order.section: Built for the future. Available today. (Get started / Contact sales)
section_order.why: Keep the final ask, but repeat the hero button text and the pricing line under it instead of a slogan-only block.

section_order.section: Changelog (Loops triggers, stacked PRs, coding agent controls, Loops for PM)
section_order.why: Dated shipping cadence reassures skeptics; it works as a closing trust signal rather than interrupting the pitch mid-page.

section_order.section: A new species of product tool (FIG 0.1 Purpose-built / 0.2 Powered by agents / 0.3 Designed for speed)
section_order.why: Cut as a standalone section: three adjectives a rival can paste. Fold the one concrete line, 'From drafting PRDs to pushing PRs', into the AI and automations intro.

needs: Free plan or trial terms (what is free, team size limit, whether a credit card is required) and the paid price per seat, for a line under the hero and final buttons
How long switching takes, e.g. importing from Jira, if the owner can state it truthfully
One customer quote with a measurable result (time saved, cycle time, tool replaced), with name, title and company
One line per logo on which team uses Linear and for what, if the logo strip is to carry context
Engineering change: remove the blur/fade-in on the hero text and lazy-load the 2,305 KB of product mockups so the headline is sharp at first paint on slow phones
